title: What training and recertification do EU aviation security staff need?
description: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998 Chapter 11: background checks, security training, screener recertification every 3 years and 6 monthly image training.
shortAnswer: Chapter 11 of the Annex to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998 sets recruitment and training rules for EU aviation security staff. Staff must complete relevant training before implementing security controls unsupervised. Screeners operating X-ray or EDS equipment must be recertified at least every 3 years and complete at least 6 hours of image recognition training every 6 months, other certified staff every 5 years, and most other security competencies need recurrent training at least every 5 years.
keyTakeaways: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998 sets the detailed measures under Regulation (EC) No 300/2008; Chapter 11 of its Annex covers recruitment, training, certification, recurrent training and instructors.

Screening, access control and other security staff in security restricted areas need an enhanced background check, repeated at least every 12 months unless an ongoing review mechanism is in place (11.1.1, 11.1.7).
Staff performing tasks in 11.2.3.1 to 11.2.3.5 need initial certification, then recertification at least every 3 years for X-ray or EDS operators and at least every 5 years for others (11.3.1).
X-ray and EDS operators complete image recognition training and testing of at least 6 hours in every 6 month period, with a performance evaluation at the end of each period (11.4.1, 11.4.2).
Other security competencies require recurrent training at least once every 5 years, or before returning to duty after more than 6 months without exercising them (11.4.3).
jurisdiction: European Union (all Member States; directly applicable regulation with EEA relevance)
regulator: European Commission under Regulation (EC) No 300/2008 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998, with each Member State's appropriate authority for aviation security approving courses and certifying staff
appliesTo: Screeners of passengers, cabin baggage, hold baggage, cargo, mail and supplies
Staff performing access control, surveillance, patrols and vehicle examinations
Airport, air carrier and entity staff needing unescorted access to security restricted areas
Aviation security instructors and EU aviation security validators

sections.heading: Who must meet the Chapter 11 standards?

blocks.text: Any authority, airport operator, air carrier or entity deploying people who implement security measures under the national civil aviation security programme must ensure those people meet Chapter 11 (point 11.0.1). [Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02015R1998-20261001) of 5 November 2015 lays down detailed measures for the common basic standards in Regulation (EC) No 300/2008 and repealed Regulation (EU) No 185/2010.
Chapter 11 distinguishes several groups, each with its own training content:

items: **Persons implementing security controls (11.2.3):** eleven job specific categories, from screening of persons and baggage (11.2.3.1) and cargo and mail (11.2.3.2) to access control and patrols (11.2.3.5), aircraft security searches, aircraft protection, baggage reconciliation and in-flight security measures by flight and cabin crew (11.2.3.11).
**Supervisors (11.2.4):** the competencies of those supervised plus legal requirements, supervisory tasks, internal quality control, emergency response and on-the-job coaching.
**Security managers (11.2.5):** legal requirements, internal, national, Union and international quality control, motivating others, and the capabilities and limitations of security equipment.
**Persons needing unescorted access to security restricted areas (11.2.6):** security awareness training before an access authorization is issued.
**Persons requiring general security awareness (11.2.7):** a shorter awareness program, completed before taking up duty.
**Persons with cyber security roles (11.2.8):** job related training on relevant cyber risks, with course content specified or approved by the appropriate authority.

sections.heading: What background checks and recruitment steps are required?

blocks.text: Recruitment rules come before training. An **enhanced background check** is required for people recruited to implement or be responsible for screening, access control or other security controls in a security restricted area, for security managers, for instructors and for EU aviation security validators (11.1.1).

items: An enhanced check establishes identity, covers criminal records in all states of residence and employment, education and gaps for at least the preceding 5 years, and covers intelligence and other relevant information held by competent national authorities (11.1.3).

A standard check covers the same identity, criminal record and employment elements without the intelligence element (11.1.4). Staff implementing security controls outside security restricted areas, people with unescorted access to secured cargo, mail and supplies, and people with administrator rights or unsupervised access to critical aviation security IT systems need either an enhanced or a standard check, as determined by the appropriate authority under national rules (11.1.2).
Where an enhanced check is required it must be fully completed before training under 11.2.3.1 to 11.2.3.5 begins (11.1.5).
Checks are subject either to an ongoing review mechanism or to repeats at intervals not exceeding 12 months for enhanced checks and three years for standard checks (11.1.7).

Recruitment includes at least a written application and an interview, an assessment of mental and physical abilities and aptitudes, and records kept for at least the duration of the contract (11.1.8 to 11.1.10).

blocks.text: Under 11.0.9, terrorist offences referred to in Directive (EU) 2017/541 are disqualifying crimes. Point 11.1.11 also requires the security programs of operators and entities to include an internal policy enhancing staff awareness and promoting security culture to address the insider threat.

sections.heading: What must aviation security training include?

blocks.text: Persons must successfully complete relevant training before being authorized to implement security controls unsupervised (11.2.1.1). Training for screeners, vehicle examiners, access control staff and supervisors must include theoretical, practical and on-the-job elements (11.2.1.2).

items: **Approved content:** course content must be specified or approved by the appropriate authority before an instructor delivers it or before a computer based course is used (11.2.1.3).

**Basic training (11.2.2):** twelve competencies, including knowledge of previous acts of unlawful interference and current threats, the legal framework, access control and identification card systems, challenging and reporting, identifying prohibited articles, responding to incidents, how human behavior affects security performance, communicating clearly and confidently, and the elements of a resilient security culture including insider threat and radicalization.
**Security awareness (11.2.6.2):** eight competencies, and each person must demonstrate understanding of all of them before receiving an unescorted access authorization (11.2.6.3).

**Prior learning:** competencies acquired before recruitment may be taken into account in assessing training needs (11.0.5), and training already received need not be repeated for another function other than for recurrent training (11.0.7).
**Records:** training records must be kept for all persons trained for at least the duration of their contract (11.2.1.4).

blocks.title: Competency means demonstration
blocks.text: Point 11.0.4 defines competency as "being able to demonstrate suitable knowledge and skills". Completion of a course is not enough on its own; the training design needs assessments that show each listed competency.

sections.heading: How often must screeners and other security staff be recertified?

blocks.text: Persons performing the tasks in 11.2.3.1 to 11.2.3.5 must pass an initial certification or approval process, then be recertified at least every 3 years if they operate X-ray or EDS equipment, and at least every 5 years otherwise (11.3.1). Staff screening supplies who are only authorized for visual checks or hand searches may be exempted.

blocks.text: Initial certification includes a theoretical test or panel interview, a practical test, and for X-ray and EDS operators a standardized image interpretation test (11.3.2). Recertification includes a theoretical test or panel interview, an evaluation of operational performance or a practical test, and the image interpretation test for X-ray and EDS operators (11.3.3).

All certification elements except the operational performance evaluation must be performed by or on behalf of the appropriate authority, and a training institute certifying on its behalf must be fully independent of operators, security providers and instructors (11.3.7). Failure to complete recertification within a reasonable timescale, "not normally exceeding 3 months", results in withdrawal of the related security entitlements (11.3.8).

sections.heading: What does recurrent training for X-ray and EDS operators involve?

blocks.text: X-ray and EDS operators must complete recurrent image recognition training and testing, either classroom or computer based, or on-the-job threat image projection (TIP) training (11.4.1). The two routes have different library requirements.

items: **Classroom or computer based:** at least 6 hours in every 6 month period, using a library of at least 1 000 images of at least 250 different threat articles in varied orientations, or the most frequently missed TIP images combined with recently captured threat articles.
**On-the-job TIP:** a TIP library of at least 6 000 images of at least 1 500 threat articles, provided the person works with the equipment for at least one third of working hours.
**Distribution:** training and testing should preferably be spread evenly over each 6 month period, or otherwise take place at the end of it.
**Evaluation:** results of the 6 monthly performance evaluation are given to the screener, recorded, used to target weaknesses, and may be considered in recertification (11.4.2).

blocks.text: For everyone else, 11.4.3(b) adds a duty to train on new or extended competencies so that staff "are promptly made aware of new threats and legal requirements by the time they have to be applied". Records of recurrent training must be kept for at least the duration of the contract (11.4.4). For scheduling, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: What qualifications must aviation security instructors hold?

blocks.text: Instructors must pass an enhanced background check and be competent in instructional techniques, knowledgeable about the relevant work environment, and competent in the security elements they teach (11.5.1). Certification applies at least to instructors teaching the 11.2.3.1 to 11.2.3.5 categories, supervisors (with a limited exception) and security managers, and instructors are recertified at least every 5 years.

Appropriate authorities keep lists of instructors and may withdraw course approval or suspend an instructor if training is not producing the required competencies (11.5.3 and 11.5.4). Instructor competencies acquired in one Member State must be recognized in another (11.5.5).

sections.heading: Is Chapter 11 current as at November 2026?

blocks.text: Yes. As at November 2026, the latest consolidated text of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1998 on EUR-Lex is dated 1 October 2026. Chapter 11 was most recently amended by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/920, which revised the certification definitions and processes, and by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/449. National aviation security programs and appropriate authorities add detailed course approvals and certification procedures, so the national program must be read alongside the regulation.

Crew security training is one of the categories in 11.2.3.11; for wider recurrent crew training under aviation safety rules, see [EU aircrew recurrent training requirements](/regulations/eu-aircrew-recurrent-training-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents each 11.2 competency list as a defined framework with assessment points, so a basic, job specific or awareness course can show which competency each item demonstrates. Shared competencies across roles are defined once, which supports the 11.0.7 rule that training already received need not be repeated for another function.

faqs.q: Can aviation security training be delivered as e-learning?
faqs.a: Computer based training is allowed, with or without an instructor or coach, but its content must be specified or approved by the appropriate authority before use (11.2.1.3). Training for screeners, vehicle examiners, access control staff and supervisors must still include practical and on-the-job elements (11.2.1.2).

faqs.q: What happens if a screener misses recertification?
faqs.a: Point 11.3.8 states that failure to undertake or successfully complete recertification or reapproval within a reasonable timescale, not normally exceeding 3 months, results in the related security entitlements being withdrawn. Employers should track recertification dates well ahead of the 3 or 5 year limits.

faqs.q: Do all airport staff need security training?
faqs.a: Persons other than passengers who need unescorted access to security restricted areas must complete security awareness training and demonstrate understanding before receiving the access authorization (11.2.6). The appropriate authority may exempt people whose access is limited to terminal areas accessible to passengers.

faqs.q: How long must aviation security training records be kept?
faqs.a: Chapter 11 requires recruitment, training, certification and recurrent training records to be kept for at least the duration of the person's contract (11.1.10, 11.2.1.4, 11.3.9 and 11.4.4). National programs may require longer retention.
